📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Major delays for Delta come just a week after a nationwide groundstop.

Major delays for Delta come just a week after a nationwide groundstop.

According to recent reports, all Delta flights in and out of Atlanta are facing significant delays on Sunday due to a problem with the system that calculates a plane’s weight and balance. Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport is Delta’s largest hub and one of the busiest airports in the world. While only Delta is impacted at the moment, disruptions at Hartsfield-Jackson could potentially affect other airports and airlines if delays continue to pile up.

The complications with Delta’s systems in Atlanta come just one week after an FAA outage led to a nationwide groundstop and thousands of canceled flights. According to The New York Times:.

Sources indicate that the system that went offline calculates the total weight of an airplane, including its airframe, fuel, passengers and their baggage. The system also allows pilots to determine the plane’s center of gravity and whether the weight is evenly distributed — data points that help ensure safe passage.

“Delta teams are using manual workarounds this morning to safely get flights departed while work continues to restore automation,” the airline remarked in a statement on Sunday.

Bitcoin Breaks Below $60K as Crypto Fear Index Hits Worst Level Since February

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (732 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Decrypt

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bitcoin broke below $60,000 on Friday, plunging through a major psychological price level as the selloff gathered pace after Anthropic’s stock market debut.
  • The daily chart highlights BTC at $59,703.72 , down 3.55% for the session after touching a low of $59,300.
  • The Fear and Greed Index chart dipped to 9, a reading classified as “extreme fear” and its lowest since February.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin broke below $60,000 on Friday, plunging through a major psychological price level as the selloff gathered pace after Anthropic’s stock market debut.

The daily chart highlights BTC at $59,703.72 , down 3.55% for the session after touching a low of $59,300.

The Fear and Greed Index chart dipped to 9, a reading classified as “extreme fear” and its lowest since February. For reference, the index was at 18 a week ago and a neutral 51 a month earlier.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Bitcoin with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

The indicator tracks crypto market sentiment on a scale from zero, or maximum fear, to 100, or extreme greed, using market data rather than individual investor surveys. Its 2026 low was 5 on February 5, compared with a yearly high of 82 on August 26.

The selling went well beyond Bitcoin. Ethereum fell 4.24%, Solana lost 6.36%, BNB slid 4.38% and XRP declined 5.53% over the same period.

In a recent development, forced selling added to the pressure. As Decrypt reported earlier Friday, roughly $727 million in leveraged crypto positions had been liquidated over 24 hours, about 86% of them bullish bets, while U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $582.2 million on Thursday.

Spot fund withdrawals did not begin with Anthropic’s IPO. By Thursday, roughly $2.9 billion in U.S. Bitcoin ETF outflows for November, alongside higher Treasury yields and expectations of tighter Federal Reserve policy.

Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut Thursday at $111.50, up 34% from the $83 IPO price, before closing at $97.17. Friday brought another decline for the Claude developer, with the stock almost losing all the prime it gained after its IPO.

The listing raised $81.34 billion through the public offering, but enthusiasm for Anthropic shares did not carry over to the companies building the AI boom.

Sources indicate that friday’s market heatmap indicates tech stock suffering in the middle of mostly green pastures. Nvidia down 3.78%, Broadcom is down 5.65%, AMD declining 5.06% and memory-chip maker Micron dropping 6.51%. Meta fell 2.21%, adding to pressure on companies spending heavily on AI infrastructure.

Sources indicate that other major stocks were doing better. Alphabet rose 2.81%, Microsoft gained 0.50% and Apple edged up 0.25%, while healthcare stocks Eli Lilly and Johnson & Johnson rose 1.21% and 1.78%, respectively. Walmart added 2.91% and Visa climbed 1.34%.

But it was not a uniform crash across the S&P 500. The tech-heavy Nasdaq was falling more sharply than the broader index, while pockets of healthcare, consumer, and financial shares remained green.

It has been revealed that bitcoin’s daily chart turned more decisively bearish after the break below $60,000. Its 50-day exponential moving average, or EMA, was below the 200-day EMA, a death-cross configuration, and spot prices were trading beneath both lines. That confirms sustained downside momentum rather than a brief intraday dip.

In a recent development, the relative strength index, or RSI, had fallen into the teens, far below the 30 threshold usually associated with oversold conditions. The average directional index, or ADX, climbed to 43.7, signaling a strong trend, with the chart’s directional readings favoring sellers. Oversold does not mean a bounce is guaranteed.

According to recent reports, the longer-range chart puts the $60,000 breakdown in context. Bitcoin traded around this area several times in 2024 and returned to it during the mid-2026 retreat, making it a visible historical price zone as well as a round-number threshold.

With $60,000 giving way, the roughly $58,000–$59,000 support area near the mid-2026 lows comes into focus. If that zone fails, the next notable historical demand area is around $55,000–$56,000, followed by the $50,000 region marked by the deeper 2024 selloff.

For bulls, $60,000 is now the first level to hold. The next hurdle is $62,000–$62,500, followed by $65,000 and heavier resistance near $68,000–$70,000. A brief bounce back above $60,000 would not, by itself, reverse the bearish trend.

According to recent reports, as of right now, Bitcoin had touched $59,300.13, confirming that sellers had pushed below the $60,000 support zone. The next test is whether that level becomes resistance on a rebound.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA VI isn’t officially available for PC, and downloading a supposed PC version could put your computer at risk of malware.
  • The only way you can play on PC right now is to use the free PlayStation Remote Play app to stream the game from your console to your computer.
  • Industry observers note that in the meantime, scammers and opportunists have wasted no time flooding the market with everything from poorly made GTA VI clones vibe-coded with AI to actively malicious, virus-riddled downloads designed to turn your PC into a crypto mining operation or steal your money and personal data.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA VI isn’t officially available for PC, and downloading a supposed PC version could put your computer at risk of malware. Rockstar has a history of making PC gamers wait their turn for titles. Red Dead Redemption 2 got its PC port a year after consoles, and GTA 5 came to PCs almost two years after launch. While there is a somewhat credible rumor that Rockstar will be bringing GTA VI to PCs early next year, there hasn’t been an official announcement from the studio.

The only way you can play on PC right now is to use the free PlayStation Remote Play app to stream the game from your console to your computer.

Industry observers note that in the meantime, scammers and opportunists have wasted no time flooding the market with everything from poorly made GTA VI clones vibe-coded with AI to actively malicious, virus-riddled downloads designed to turn your PC into a crypto mining operation or steal your money and personal data. Cybersecurity provider Kaspersky reported recording 27,416 detections of GTA VI-related malware and unwanted apps since June.

Also: PlayStation Remote Play lets you stream GTA VI to your PC or smart TV.

In a recent development, you’ll probably be able to spot the majority of GTA VI scams a mile away, but you’re never immune to an official-looking web page or the promise of a free copy of the game. No matter how official a download page seems, unless the news is coming from Rockstar itself, you’re being lied to. And definitely take any and all claims of the game code being dumped and cracked for PC with a very large grain of salt.

But all is not lost if you got fooled into downloading a fake version of GTA VI — cleaning up and protecting your PC is a fairly straightforward process.

It has been revealed that alright, so you’ve downloaded a fake version of GTA VI. What now? Your very first move should be to immediately uninstall the program. Getting rid of the software limits a scammer’s or hacker’s options for hijacking your PC. But you can’t stop there.

Sources indicate that also: Can your PC run GTA VI? The minimum RAM, GPU, and CPU requirements to expect.

In a recent development, the fake GTA VI program itself might be gone now, but it could still be hiding malicious files deep inside your PC and wreaking havoc. Running antivirus software like AVG Avast, even the free version, can help track them all down for quarantine and destruction.

Check out our tested picks for the best antivirus protection here.

A “cracked” PC program is any software whose copy protection has been circumvented and removed. A keygen is a program that reverse-engineers the license validation algorithm your PC uses to generate fake but official-looking product keys. Both processes are heavily involved in the software pirating and sharing community, and you’ll be able to find hundreds of users across dozens of less-than-legal forums claiming to have dumped the source code for GTA VI and cracked it, making it available for PC users and modders.

Also: Lost or stolen Windows laptop? IT can lock it down without wiping it now.

While a few might actually be trying to distribute the game for free, no strings attached, most will likely have a host of malware hiding inside to hijack your PC.

As my grandfather used to say: If it smells like b.s., it is. The vast majority of GTA VI download scams fall apart under the slightest bit of scrutiny, so don’t be afraid to follow the money, as it were.

Also: 5 USB cables and dongles that can fry hardware and steal your data – or worse.

Notorious software cracker/leaker Cyberleek is claiming to have the entire source code for the Xbox build of GTA VI and will release it on Nov. 23 — but only if his scammy crypto coin hits $15 million in market cap. And while this is an obvious money-making scheme, others might not be so open about their goals. The best policy is to block, report, and keep scrolling.

  • Jensen Huang is considering a comeback as Nvidia’s chief executive, as allies in Silicon Valley pressure the company’s board to reinstate him days after the tech executive resigned over reports he had affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and a subordinate.
  • Huang has discussed with confidants the possibility of returning, according to multiple people familiar with the matter—even as an independent probe by Nvidia’s board investigates the conduct that led to a spectacular leadership crisis at the $4 trillion chip firm this week.
  • One Huang ally told the FT they were putting together a “war room” of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for the former Nvidia chief’s return and would try to garner support from the White House.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jensen Huang is considering a comeback as Nvidia’s chief executive, as allies in Silicon Valley pressure the company’s board to reinstate him days after the tech executive resigned over reports he had affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and a subordinate.

Huang has discussed with confidants the possibility of returning, according to multiple people familiar with the matter—even as an independent probe by Nvidia’s board investigates the conduct that led to a spectacular leadership crisis at the $4 trillion chip firm this week.

One Huang ally told the FT they were putting together a “war room” of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for the former Nvidia chief’s return and would try to garner support from the White House.

It has been revealed that “Everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen,” they remarked. The efforts had Huang’s support, they added.

Sources indicate that A public campaign to reinstate Huang has gathered steam over the weekend. Tesla and SpaceX chief Elon Musk and Epic Games chief executive Tim Sweeney were among executives backing a public letter demanding that its board “Bring Jensen Back.”.

Huang continues to command fierce loyalty from some employees, several of whom have gone public in calling for his return in the days since he resigned and have signed the open letter.

The effort to reinstate Huang is likely to face pushback from key policymakers in Washington, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday calling for a “dramatic shake-up” in leadership at the company after Huang’s departure.

Huang, who lacked the controlling shareholding of other founder-CEOs and was therefore unable to overule any board decision, also faces a board and a management team now led by interim chief executive Colette Kress that is aiming to steady the tech giant ahead of quarterly results on Tuesday.

Huang’s affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, has triggered deepening scrutiny of Nvidia’s compliance measures when selling its AI chips to customers in Asia who have potential links to China.

Even allies were unsure how to rehabilitate Huang’s reputation. “Having an affair with a subordinate is a fireable offense,” acknowledged one person involved in efforts to reinstate Huang.

According to recent reports, the FT reported on Friday that Arm chief Rene Haas has been approached by Nvidia’s board as a potential successor. Nvidia’s board stated no “formal” process had been initiated.

Altimeter Capital founder Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management boss Gavin Baker—who are Nvidia shareholders—published an open letter to the board on Friday urging them to leave “all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang.”.

The pair, both large investors in the company, cited “the extraordinary success of Jensen Huang’s leadership over a long period of time and given the massive uncertainty associated with recent events surrounding his departure” as reasons for clemency.

US moves to cut China’s remote access to AI chips

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1251 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On the heels of the Nvidia scandal, the Trump administration is preparing to crack down on foreign data centers that are fueling China’s advancements in artificial intelligence by allowing remote access to otherwise restricted high-end chips necessary for AI training.
  • In a summary of the rule change, the Commerce Department remarked it was closing a loophole that previously allowed foreign rivals like China, Russia, and Iran to bypass export curbs on certain advanced computer chips by instead renting access to those chips from data centers in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil.
  • US rivals could possibly use that access to train and run advanced AI models “capable of supporting military- and intelligence-related activities that could threaten US national security or foreign policy interests,” the Commerce Department remarked.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On the heels of the Nvidia scandal, the Trump administration is preparing to crack down on foreign data centers that are fueling China’s advancements in artificial intelligence by allowing remote access to otherwise restricted high-end chips necessary for AI training.

In a summary of the rule change, the Commerce Department remarked it was closing a loophole that previously allowed foreign rivals like China, Russia, and Iran to bypass export curbs on certain advanced computer chips by instead renting access to those chips from data centers in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil.

US rivals could possibly use that access to train and run advanced AI models “capable of supporting military- and intelligence-related activities that could threaten US national security or foreign policy interests,” the Commerce Department remarked. Among threats, the US fears rivals could use advanced AI to develop “more effective weapons of mass destruction and advanced conventional weapons, coordinated cyber-espionage and targeted cyber-disruption, algorithmic theft, and weaponized disinformation.”.

Now, the rules have been tightened up so much that the South China Morning Post reported that, “as a result, any advanced chips made for a Chinese firm are assumed to be restricted, and factories must ask the US government for a license before shipping them.”.

The rule change takes effect 90 days after it’s posted to the Federal Register. Moving forward, companies headquartered in any of those countries deemed to “present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion” to China, Russia, and Iran must apply for a license with strict know-your-customer controls when transferring high volumes of advanced chips. If a license is granted, companies will have to “perform robust due diligence,” submitting monthly reports on transactions that thoroughly detail all parties involved, as well as their parent companies, and the final destination for chips sold.

In a press release Sunday, the Commerce Department described the rule change as “designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centers in third countries.” An exception was carved out for companies providing computing power “exclusively used for commercial recommender systems.” The Department said it was acting to “prevent certain foreign actors from leveraging advanced computing power based on US technology to threaten US national security and foreign policy interests.”.

Without the intervention, officials fear that China could develop a military or economic edge, The Upcoming York Times reported.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned after admitting to an affair with a woman, Alice Huang, suspected of serving as a Chinese spy. Congress is probing if Alice Huang used her personal relationship with Jensen Huang to help her former company, Megaspeed, become one of Nvidia’s biggest customers, then used that position to smuggle Nvidia’s restricted AI chips into China. China has denied that Alice Huang was a spy, and Megaspeed has denied that smuggling occurred, while launching its own internal probe.

In a recent development, megaspeed is a Singaporean data center firm whose primary business is cloud computing and AI infrastructure. Prior to the rule change, selling remote access to AI servers to customers in China was perfectly legal, NYT noted. But now, the Commerce Department has given firms like Megaspeed 90 days to either obtain licenses or face future export restrictions.

In a recent development, whether or not to add more chip curbs has been a polarizing debate in the Trump administration. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent reportedly butted heads with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. When the Megaspeed news broke, Bessent pushed for curbs, but Lutnick reportedly appeared “too cozy” with Nvidia to move. Instead, Lutnick initially favored looser controls that Nvidia claimed would ensure global dominance of US technology. (A Commerce Department spokesperson told NYT that Bessent has never confronted Lutnick over his handling of Megaspeed.).

Any companies found violating the rules could face a “range of consequences,” the Commerce Department noted after reportedly bending to Bessent’s pressure campaign. Those include possibly facing new import restrictions, stricter license requirements, downgrading their status in the US export control regime, or other changes to their company’s or their base country’s entity-list designations.

Although the summary of the rule change remarked that “Commerce will be actively monitoring for countries that tolerate evasion” of the anti-diversion policy, it’s unclear how aggressively the Commerce Department might enforce the rule, NYT noted.

Bessent has publicly criticized Lutnick for failing to sanction Megaspeed, and NYT reported that ultimately, enforcement of the stricter rules—which Bessent helped draft—“would be up to the Commerce Department.”.

Industry observers note that “The real story here should be: Did Nvidia know their client, and was there a robust effort at Nvidia to make sure that there was no leakage and that they were selling to what were obviously pass-through shell companies?” Bessent mentioned on a CNBC appearance. “I think it’s notable that anyone at the company there be held accountable for that.”.

Industry observers note that there’s even a push to oust Lutnick over his position on chips, but The Guardian reported that Donald Trump confirmed he has no prepares to replace the AI industry-friendly commerce secretary. On Monday, Trump told reporters that Lutnick was right to delay blacklisting Megaspeed, because “if you didn’t delay it… you could have a blow-up with China.”.

Recent findings suggest that at the press gaggle, Trump aligned with China in saying that there’s no evidence yet that Alice Huang was a spy. He also joined a band of prominent tech leaders calling for Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia, saying that it wasn’t a “bad idea.”.

According to recent reports, “Nobody’s proven that she’s a spy,” Trump said. “She may not be a spy.”.

However, US investigators have alleged that they found “Alice Huang used industry contacts and a series of shell companies to access 240,000 chips banned for export into China,” CBS News reported.

China is unlikely to welcome the fresh rules, as it has consistently accused the US of fabricating the spying claims to justify imposing additional chip restrictions.

However, a senior Trump official, granted anonymity to discuss sensitive policy matters, told the NYT that Trump “did not expect countermeasures from China in response.”.

Trump will be in China for an economic summit this week, including a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. The newly introduced curbs could potentially disrupt those talks, according to Hong Yuan, a researcher and secretary-general of the Center for American Military Studies at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences. Hong told the People’s Daily that China will likely view the rule change as politically motivated.

It has been revealed that “Before any judicial causality was established, Washington handed down a political conviction, substituting suspicion for proof, espionage for personal contact, and an industrial embargo for private conduct,” Hong said. “The matter is not the cause of tighter controls, but a political catalyst.”.

The latest policy could hurt the US, experts told the Chinese outlets. Analysts told the South China Morning Post that the policy could “accelerate Chinese companies’ shift to domestic AI chips.” Other experts told the People’s Daily—which is the official newspaper of the Chinese Communist Party—that “the cost of switching back to US platforms will rise” over time. If that happened, it could potentially lock in Chinese technology over America’s in “the world’s largest single consumer market for chips,” experts remarked.

Sun Chenghao, senior fellow at the Center for International Security and Strategy at Tsinghua University in Beijing, told the People’s Daily that “what US companies stand to lose could be customers and technological influence for years to come.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A humanoid robotics organization backed and advised by President Donald Trump’s son, Eric Trump, has reportedly missed payroll and may be on the brink of collapse after a funding shortfall. The Silicon Valley startup, Foundation Future Industries, claims it is developing and testing robots for military roles on battlefields from Ukraine to Gaza.

Foundation failed to pay employees for the payroll period ending on October 30, anonymous sources told CNBC. The startup’s staff is especially angry because Foundation’s co-founder and CEO, Sankaet Pathak, supposedly borrowed $4.6 million in company funds to buy a luxury home overlooking San Francisco Bay about a year ago.

This comes as Pathak and Foundation’s leadership are still looking to raise funding to support a $3 billion valuation, based on their promise to develop a humanoid robot ready for combat duty and capable of wielding various weapons.

It has been revealed that the organization has demonstrated a humanoid robot named the Phantom MK-1 and is touting an upcoming robot called the Phantom MK-2. Foundation has touted its humanoid robots for roles in warehouses and other workplaces—but has courted media coverage by claiming it is developing humanoid robots for battlefield use.

Now CNBC’s reporting based on “people with direct knowledge of the matter” indicates that insiders worry the startup could soon collapse without additional funding.

It has been revealed that eric Trump holds an equity stake in Foundation and was announced as its chief strategy advisor in March 2026, according to the Financial Times. Investment funds linked to both Eric Trump and Donald Trump Jr. are involved with multiple military technology companies that have received Pentagon loans and contracts worth more than $3.2 billion as of July 2026, according to The Washington Post.

After Trump claimed that Foundation had “just secured a $24 million contract with the Pentagon” during the Fox Business interview in April, Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) responded by questioning whether the Pentagon is “just a cash machine for Trump’s kids now” in a social media post. “This looks like corruption in plain sight,” Warren wrote.

In a recent development, but publicly available evidence does not back up Trump’s claim about Foundation directly receiving US government funding. Federal spending records show that Foundation holds no publicly listed contracts, according to The San Francisco Standard.

Instead, the organization Boardwalk Robotics received four contracts worth $3.22 million prior to being acquired by Foundation in late 2024.

Meanwhile, the Institute for Human & Machine Cognition—a Florida-based nonprofit research institute and research partner to Boardwalk Robotics—secured a $24.8 million Navy contract in 2025, The San Francisco Standard reported.

This was not the first time that Foundation’s leadership and investors have made unsupported statements. In 2024, General Motors pushed back on Foundation’s claims that it was about to get an investment from the Detroit automaker, according to CNBC.

In a recent development, on November 11, 2026, Mike LeBlanc, co-founder and president of Foundation Future Industries, told the Financial Times that the manufacturer was in talks with the Israeli military to provide humanoid robots for patrol and combat duties in Hamas tunnels beneath Gaza. He also described taking the company’s Phantom MK1 humanoid robot along to tour some of the tunnels.

However, the Israeli defense ministry declined to comment when the Financial Times reached out.

LeBlanc also previously claimed that two of the organization’s Phantom MK-1 units went to Ukraine for testing in frontline reconnaissance and logistics roles in February 2026.

Sources indicate that but Craig Smith, an independent journalist and host of the podcast Eye on AI, described tagging along during the delivery of the Phantom robots to Ukraine. He said that the robots never made it to Ukraine because they were stopped at the border with Poland.

When questioned by Smith, LeBlanc only remarked that Foundation had conducted a pilot demonstration at an undisclosed location, without clarifying whether the robots ever reached Ukraine. LeBlanc also walked back a claim that Foundation had demonstrated its humanoid robots to the Ukrainian government organization Brave1.

According to recent reports, promotional videos showing Foundation’s humanoids have not provided evidence that the robots are ready for battlefield deployments. For example, a “mortar demo” video on the firm website dated to May 2026 highlights a person handing a mortar shell to one of the humanoid robots, which slowly lowers the shell over the muzzle of a mortar weapon before finally dropping it in.

Whatever happens to Foundation, humanoid robots remain largely unproven technology and have yet to fulfill manufacturer promises that they can become general-purpose robots handling many different tasks. Companies have just begun testing and deploying such robots in greater numbers within relatively controlled environments such as factories and warehouses.

Similarly, humanoid robots have not yet had any impact on the battlefield. Instead, pioneers in robotics warfare, like the Ukrainian military, have focused on developing and deploying unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs)—robotic vehicles that roll along on wheels or tank-style caterpillar tracks.

While defending against the Russian invasion of Ukraine, the Ukrainian military has increasingly deployed more ground robots along with swarms of flying drones to make up for a shortfall in human soldiers compared to Russia. Such ground robots have typically been tasked with performing risky supply runs or evacuating wounded soldiers from frontline positions, but have also entered combat while wielding projectile weapons or even explosives when equipped as roving bombs.

According to recent reports, most recently, Ukraine has deployed armed ground robots directly into combat through both amphibious landings and through airdrops. In 2026, part of Ukraine’s counteroffensive success in rolling back Russian territorial gains has included dropping military robots from drones in airborne assaults behind Russian frontline positions.

#21780. Echo Studio with Home Camera review: An excellent speaker – if you’re OK with being tracked

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (970 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Zdnet ↗ Open Full Page

Echo Studio with Home Camera review: An excellent speaker – if you’re OK with being tracked

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (970 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Echo Studio, Amazon’s flagship smart speaker, just got an upgrade that includes a Home Camera.
  • Also: Apple HomeView review: The deep ecosystem integration wins again.
  • Recent findings suggest that I tested the latest Echo Studio with Home Camera to see how it performs in my smart home.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Echo Studio, Amazon’s flagship smart speaker, just got an upgrade that includes a Home Camera. It’s not just for watching what’s going on in your house while you’re away; the camera also tracks your location to adjust audio volume depending on where you are. Is this a privacy nightmare or the speaker of your dreams? The answer is not quite so simple.

Also: Apple HomeView review: The deep ecosystem integration wins again.

Recent findings suggest that I tested the latest Echo Studio with Home Camera to see how it performs in my smart home. I was (and still am) skeptical of the camera, but after a few days, I grew increasingly pleased with the audio quality and tracking features the more I used it and compared it with other speakers. Ultimately, it’s these things that make the speaker stand out for me.

The Echo Studio supports Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3, and serves as a smart home hub for Alexa with Zigbee, Matter, and Thread compatibility, and can also serve as an Eero extender. If you have a home theater setup or a Fire TV, the Echo Studio can also be integrated into your existing system, syncing up to five Echo Studio or Echo Dot Max speakers — all of one type; you can’t mix and match.

Personally, I don’t keep indoor security cameras except for one to watch my dog while I’m out, and that’s only on when no one else is at home. I’m the type to cover all the cameras on my Echo Show devices and laptops, because I don’t like the idea of having a connected device that can record in the privacy of my home, the only place where my kids and family are safe from being unwillingly displayed online.

Because of this, I didn’t quite see the need for an Echo Studio with a Home Camera. However, I admit there are plenty of uses for it, and many smart homes across the US and around the world already have indoor security cameras, so there’s a definite market for this speaker.

Also: Echo Dot (2026) review: The best compact Amazon speaker yet – but it’ll cost you.

The Echo Studio lets you “drop in” to the camera whenever you want to see what’s happening in the room it’s in (and when the camera is on, of course). This is a useful feature if you’re away from home and want to check in on your empty house.

But it’s not a full-fledged security camera. You can’t remotely move the Echo Studio to adjust the angle, for example. So you won’t be able to face it toward the wall for privacy, as you can with a pan/tilt indoor security camera. If you do decide to have your camera face away, you’d have to move the entire Echo Studio speaker, which would lose much of the speaker’s front-firing audio depth.

Industry observers note that the Echo Studio has a button to enable or disable the microphone and camera simultaneously, but you can’t turn one off or on without the other. In other words, you can’t just record audio or just video. The camera also has a dedicated status LED so you can see when it’s running, even if it’s not recording.

The Echo Studio is an excellent speaker for medium and large rooms, as well as open spaces in the home. The Home Camera is meant to complete an immersive sound environment that tracks movement and adjusts volume to match your position in the room. The feature that matches the volume to your location as you move proved to be perfect for listening to music and audiobooks while I cleaned. I moved around picking up clutter, dusting, and vacuuming to test it, and the sound tracking was pretty satisfying.

Industry observers note that the sound from the Echo Studio is rich, full, and crisp. It keeps the vocals clear and the bass deep without rattling, and I’d say it’s comparable to the audio from the Sonos Era 100, but with stronger bass.

Also: Apple HomePod Mini 2 first look: Siri has improved, but it’s a fierce AI assistant race.

According to recent reports, music is one thing, but listening to audiobooks and podcasts on a speaker while you move around can make you miss parts when you get too far along. The Echo Studio with Home Camera solved this problem.

Recent findings suggest that you can also use the camera to leverage Alexa+’s visual intelligence features by showing it something and asking Alexa to tell you more about it. I wasn’t very successful with this feature, but it might be because the lighting in my office is atrocious (Amazon does say you need good lighting to do this).

The Echo Studio with Home Camera is perfect for consumers who appreciate a powerful speaker that doubles as a smart home hub, especially if you have an Eero system or a Fire TV.

When it comes down to it, Amazon built a very capable speaker for Alexa-centric homes in the Echo Studio, and added what could be a leg up with the Home Camera — if you’re into that sort of thing. The camera can be a fun feature for audio tracking and to check in on your pets while you’re out, but there are caveats.

Also: Is your TV tracking what you watch? 4 ways to limit it, starting with ACR.

In a recent development, not everyone will be a fan of having a camera attached to their speaker, especially one that doesn’t have a physical cover. If you like the idea of an Alexa+ speaker that lets you interact visually with the virtual assistant and includes a camera you can check in on, the Echo Studio with Home Camera is a good choice.

If immediate patching is not feasible, implement temporary compensating controls, such as restricting and validating Base64 input at the application boundary, enforcing input-size limits, and limiting unauthenticated access.Review Oracle’s security advisory for guidance on patching and affected products and versions. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An Anthropic mathematician says Claude helped him crack the Riemann hypothesis, a 167-year-old puzzle with a $1 million prize attached.

His claim surfaced Friday, one day after the AI firm’s stock-market debut, and has not yet been independently verified.

According to recent reports, “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Levent Alpöge wrote in a four-page note. He says the method also resolves the broader Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, which extends the question to other mathematical functions.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Anthropic with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

Recent findings suggest that alpöge states he and Claude encoded their argument in Lean, software used to check mathematical proofs step by step. His note links to 14 downloadable parts of the proof archive, but its availability does not amount to acceptance by the mathematical community.

Alpöge claims he messaged Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei about a possible announcement “late Sunday night,” November 15. He then consulted company leadership and remarked there was a constraint to respect, without explaining precisely what it was.

“The precise timing is horrible,” he acknowledged. Alpöge rejected a cynical interpretation of the timing, but did not explicitly say the company’s IPO caused the delay.

Anthropic began trading on Nasdaq Thursday, November 19, after raising $81.34 billion in its offering.

Alpöge figured in September’s AI math wars. OpenAI claimed it had solved the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem as he and NYU mathematician Tristan Buckmaster pursued related fluid-equation work, sparking a credit dispute over research priority.

Sources indicate that openAI followed in October with 722 manuscripts generated by an unreleased model, grouped into 372 families of results. Only 162 included Lean-checked main results, and mathematicians demanded stronger evidence rather than accepting the company’s flood of claims at face value.

It has been revealed that some mathematicians fear a “mathocalypse,” with AI solving coveted problems before researchers can learn from pursuing them. Toronto mathematician Daniel Litt warned that, without adaptation, “there’s just no more math in 50 years.” At an MIT panel this week, Buckmaster argued mathematics still requires human understanding.

Sources indicate that first posed by Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis predicts where certain zeros of the Riemann zeta function fall. The question matters because those zeros are linked to the distribution of prime numbers, whose patterns underlie extensive mathematical research.

A proof would be a historic mathematical result, since experts have been trying to solve that for over a century.

Lean can verify that formal deductions obey its rules. Mathematicians still need to reproduce the archive, check the formalized theorem matches the original conjecture, and examine the claimed result before considering it settled.

Industry observers note that anthropic previously reported progress on the zeta function without claiming to solve the full hypothesis. Alpöge’s upcoming assertion goes far beyond that earlier work.

Sources indicate that the Clay Mathematics Institute lists the Riemann hypothesis among its Millennium Prize Problems, each carrying a $1 million award. Under the institute’s prize rules, a proposed solution must be published in a qualifying outlet, survive at least two years of scrutiny, and earn general acceptance before the prize can be considered.

#21773. Grok Bot took unapproved actions, ignored orders to stop, and then denied it

Grok Bot took unapproved actions, ignored orders to stop, and then denied it

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (742 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that researchers recently discovered unexpected behavior from Grok Bot, the AI agent platform from Elon Musk’s SpaceXSI.
  • It has been revealed that the behavior was reported Tuesday by NewCore, the maker of a managed gateway product that acts as an intermediary between AI agents and the tools and accounts they are assigned to work with.
  • According to recent reports, once the employees learned that Grok Bot had tried to check in with accounts without prompting, one of them instructed the agent, four separate times, to stop taking any actions on its own.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that researchers recently discovered unexpected behavior from Grok Bot, the AI agent platform from Elon Musk’s SpaceXSI. Over five days, Grok bots installed on two separate employee laptops made 31 requests to access data stored in employee calendar, email, Slack, and GitHub accounts. The bots performed the actions even though the employees had never ordered them and continued doing them even after employees instructed them to stop. The bots also denied having taken the actions at all.

It has been revealed that the behavior was reported Tuesday by NewCore, the maker of a managed gateway product that acts as an intermediary between AI agents and the tools and accounts they are assigned to work with. In some cases, the unapproved access attempts occurred while the laptop with Grok Bot installed had its lid shut, or late at night while the employee was sleeping. None of the unprompted actions were recorded in Grok logs. Without the gateway logs, the employees would have had no idea they occurred. And of course, without the gateway, the unapproved accesses would have succeeded—again without the end user’s knowledge.

According to recent reports, once the employees learned that Grok Bot had tried to check in with accounts without prompting, one of them instructed the agent, four separate times, to stop taking any actions on its own. The agent’s reply was: “I won’t set that up, and I’ll stop offering recurring check-ins.” Despite acknowledging the explicit instructions, the Grok Bot made more unapproved access attempts. When one of the employees asked the bot if it made any accesses, it checked twice and then outputted: “Overnight into Friday morning I was idle.”.

Industry observers note that the NewCore employees sent the gateway logs to Grok Bot support personnel and asked what was causing the bots to access accounts without prompting or approval. The support team’s reply indicated the behavior was by design and intended to allow the bots to proactively take actions on behalf of consumers. In other words, the unrequested and unlogged access attempts were a feature designed to make Grok Bot more useful by periodically checking in and finding tasks to perform before a user even asks. The proactive check-in is a feature of Cursor, the AI coding service SpaceXSI recently acquired.

In a recent development, “There is no bug to patch, which is exactly why this is worse than a bug,” Ido Hoorvitch, a NewCore security researcher, wrote in an email. “A vulnerability gets fixed. This is the product working as designed: an agent that holds your credentials, acts under your identity while you sleep, ignores the one refusal you can give it, and then tells you it did nothing.”.

Hoorvitch remarked that Grok Bot provides minimal notification of the automatic “turns,” or the cycles that occur when an agent receives instructions or context, decides what to do, and calls whatever tools it chooses. The notice comes during onboarding when the bot says it keeps working while the user is away from the computer and connects to apps and uses them the way the user does.

Recent findings suggest that “It reads like a welcome message and scrolls off the screen in under a minute,” Hoorvitch noted. “Nobody is asked to consent to it. Nothing indicates the platform will start turns with no message from you, or that those turns will use your connectors.”.

The researcher said that Grok Bot documentation notes that a primary bot checks in on its own, and a changelog mentions brief background wakes, but there is no mention that the check-ins “reach into your connected apps.” Further, once a check-in runs, there is no mention of it in the chat interface or in the chat history, and as already noted, prompts to stop check-ins don’t work. Hoorvitch said the bot “always asks before making changes,” but that applies only to events in which data or changes are written to an app.

It has been revealed that newCore contacted Grok Bot support on November 4. At the time, customers had no way to turn off the automatic check-ins. Then, eight days later, Hoorvitch stated, the Cursor dashboard, the administrative console behind Grok Bot, received an upgrade. Under bot capabilities, a new toggle called proactive messages appeared. By default, it’s set to on. When a team admin sets it to off, bots no longer run check-ins on their own.

SpaceXSI representatives didn’t answer questions sent by email.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the most anticipated game of the last two decades is finally here, but Rockstar has yet to announce an official PC release date or system requirements for GTA VI. GamesBeat claims to have confirmed that a port will arrive sometime in Q1 2027. Either way, you have plenty of time to make sure your build is ready.

Also: Fake GTA downloads are flooding the web – how not to get scammed.

Sources indicate that based on my experience with gaming PCs and the hardware requirements of similar games, I estimate that GTA VI’s minimum PC requirements could include 16GB of RAM, an Nvidia GTX 1060 or AMD Radeon RX 480 GPU, and an Intel Core i7-4770K or AMD Ryzen 5 1500X CPU. GTA VI shares a lot of technological DNA with Red Dead Redemption 2, which I used as a reference to estimate the minimum PC system requirements needed to run GTA VI at reasonable settings.

I’ll walk you through the PS5 and Xbox Series X|S specs, as well as the known requirements for RDR2, to help you decide if an upgrade is needed.

The full download file size for GTA VI tops out at 223GB on PS5, making it more than double the size of GTA V Enhanced on PC (105GB) and roughly 1.5 times bigger than RDR2 (150GB). So if you’ve been trying to scrape by with a 256GB or 512GB storage drive, I strongly advise you to upgrade to at least a 1TB SSD for GTA VI. This not only gives you plenty of breathing room for other crucial programs and files on your PC, but an SSD will also give you faster loading times than a traditional HDD, which is an absolute requirement for the texture-heavy, sun-drenched tropical visuals of GTA VI.

Both the PS5 and Xbox Series X|S use custom AMD Zen 2 8-core proprietary CPUs and AMD Radeon RDNA 2 graphics processors, which is great news for PC gamers running older rigs. When a game is ported to PC, it has to be optimized for the lowest common denominator, and there are plenty of gamers out there running older 8-core Intel and AMD CPUs.

Also: How to play GTA VI on your PC today – with a free app.

So, there is hope that the minimum CPU and graphics card requirements will be low enough that most PC builds from the last five years will be able to handle GTA VI on at least medium settings.

Since RDR2 and GTA VI share a lot of the same gameplay systems and game engines, I can get a much better idea of what kind of PC build you’ll need by looking at the requirements listed on RDR2’s Steam store page.

According to recent reports, red Dead Redemption 2 requires at least an Intel i5-2500K or AMD FX-6300 CPU, 8GB of RAM, and either an Nvidia GTX 770 or AMD Radeon R9 280 graphics card. These are fairly old components, so if you’re rocking a build kitted out with them, don’t expect to be able to push your game past baseline specs for frame rate or visuals.

Also: Best early Black Friday gaming laptop deals.

In a recent development, if you want the full experience, you’ll need at least an Intel Core i7 or AMD Ryzen 5 1500 processor, 12GB of RAM, and an Nvidia GTX 1060 or AMD Radeon RX 480 to meet RDR2’s recommended requirements. A lot of gaming PC builds you can buy now are outfitted with at least an RTX 30 series or AMD Radeon 8000 series graphics card and a CPU that was released within the last generation, so if you need a complete overhaul, it’s fairly easy to find a prebuilt rig at a reasonable price.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, drone and missile strikes have inflicted unprecedented damage on data centers in Eastern Europe and the Middle East this year, disrupting cloud services for millions of people and permanently deleting some Amazon Web Services customer data.
  • According to recent reports, to explore what this all means for modern society’s reliance on cloud resilience, I will be hosting a live conversation titled “Drone attacks and data centers: Latest Risks for Big Tech” on Tuesday, November 17 at 1 pm ET with Joseph Jarnecki, a senior research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), a UK defense and security think tank.
  • Jarnecki has done extensive research on how Ukraine strengthened its cloud resilience with Western partners despite facing both cyberattacks and kinetic attacks at the start of the full-scale Russian invasion, and explored what that means for NATO and European governments’ cloud adoption prepares.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, drone and missile strikes have inflicted unprecedented damage on data centers in Eastern Europe and the Middle East this year, disrupting cloud services for millions of people and permanently deleting some Amazon Web Services customer data. This trend represents a newly introduced concern for Big Tech companies—but also for governments and everyone else who depends on common digital services in modern life.

According to recent reports, to explore what this all means for modern society’s reliance on cloud resilience, I will be hosting a live conversation titled “Drone attacks and data centers: Latest Risks for Big Tech” on Tuesday, November 17 at 1 pm ET with Joseph Jarnecki, a senior research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), a UK defense and security think tank. He leads RUSI’s work on how cloud services factor into national security and defense, along with tech sovereignty efforts.

Jarnecki has done extensive research on how Ukraine strengthened its cloud resilience with Western partners despite facing both cyberattacks and kinetic attacks at the start of the full-scale Russian invasion, and explored what that means for NATO and European governments’ cloud adoption prepares.

This year, Jarnecki has written about Iran’s drone and missile strikes on Amazon data centers in the Middle East during the US-Israeli war with Iran, and the broader implications for governments and Big Tech. He has also commented on the impacts of Russia and Ukraine exchanging strikes on each other’s data centers.

For more background on the data center attacks that have transpired so far in 2026, you can see my previous Ars coverage of how the Iranian strikes left Amazon with months of repairs, and caused enough damage to result in the permanent loss of some AWS customer data.

I’ve also covered why Russia was not ready for the data center war it started with Ukraine, with the systematic Russian strike campaign targeting Ukraine’s data centers provoking Ukrainian counterstrikes that damaged Russian government data centers and AI data centers owned by the Russian tech giant Yandex.

My conversation with Jarnecki will explore why data centers have become much more prominent military targets, whether defending or hardening data centers against drones and missiles is a realistic option, how cloud resiliency can be improved in wartime conditions, and the choices governments and cloud providers face in deploying data centers during an era of growing geopolitical risks.

You can watch the discussion live on YouTube on November 17 at 1 pm ET. We will also be fielding a few audience questions.

#21763. Flowtica Verso vs. Comulytic Note Pro: This one wins on speed – and price

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1496 w)

Flowtica Verso vs. Comulytic Note Pro: This one wins on speed – and price

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1496 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that we primarily interact with AI via our phones and computers, but there’s a growing subset of devices that act as a go-between.
  • Also: The Flowtica Verso AI notetaker is my fresh favorite MagSafe gadget.
  • The Verso is a standalone device, but it also has a MagSafe connector so you can attach it to the back of your smartphone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that we primarily interact with AI via our phones and computers, but there’s a growing subset of devices that act as a go-between. The new Flowtica Verso is one such device. And it’s got something that’s new to this class of device — a big touchscreen display.

Also: The Flowtica Verso AI notetaker is my fresh favorite MagSafe gadget.

The Verso is a standalone device, but it also has a MagSafe connector so you can attach it to the back of your smartphone. Yes, that means yet another screen, which can be a lot to ask. I recently tested the Verso to see if it does what it says, and compared it to Comulytic’s Note Pro, a device I reviewed favorably earlier this year.

Recent findings suggest that I’m old enough to have been taught a bunch of now obsolete skills, shorthand being one. Another skill that’s come and gone is dictation and transcription. I owned several recorders over the years — from tape to digital — and used them extensively.

I use them, however, because a close encounter with a disease-ridden Scottish tick left me with a bit of cramping and neuropathy in my hands, ultimately nudging me toward investigating more non-keyboard options for my phone.

Sources indicate that aside from being potential time-savers, AI voice recorders are a next-generation accessibility solution. After all, we’re all one misfortune away from needing something to make the digital world more accessible.

I’ve tried quite a few AI voice recorders, and to date my favorite has been the Comulytic Note Pro, which doesn’t have the Verso’s big e-paper display and currently costs $130. I’ve used this more than I thought I would, but I have to admit that it still hasn’t integrated itself into my workflow in a way that makes it a must-have.

Also: I cloned my voice with free AI tools – and tested a scam call on my family.

Now that I’ve used both for a while, I think I can offer some grist for the mill for anyone on the fence about whether they want an AI voice recorder with or without an e-paper touchscreen.

In a recent development, both the Flowtica Verso and Comulytic’s Note Pro are excellent. Despite the Verso having twice as many microphones as the Note Pro (four compared to two, plus a dedicated conduction mic for recording phone calls), I really can’t find a significant difference in recording quality between the two.

The Comulytic Note Pro is smaller, thinner, and lighter, and feels more like a finder card than a recorder. There’s a button to start recording and a tiny 0.8-inch LCD status display to keep you in the loop. And it offers a quite decent battery life of 45 hours (and 107 days on standby). The Note Pro is simple; all you need to worry about is keeping it charged and pressing the button to start recording.

I want to like the Verso. It’s a nice bit of hardware with a premium, durable feel, and it comes packed with the promise of making my life easier. And some aspects of the device work well. Its voice pickup — even when multiple people are talking — is unnervingly accurate, and the transcription is excellent.

Also: My 3 favorite AI tools for voice dictation while vibe coding.

It has been revealed that it’s also very good at recording phone conversations, though I noticed that using a phone case can reduce accuracy. I’m assuming that this gives the conduction mic, which uses vibration to pick up the other side of phone conversations, less to go on. Battery life is excellent as well, and I have no problem believing Flowtica’s 70-hour runtime claim.

The Verso is slow. Really, painfully slow.

With the Note Pro, you press a button, and off you go. With the Verso, there’s a noticeable lag as you sit there waiting for the screen to refresh and the action to kick off.

Also: 5 ways I use ChatGPT Work to save time and money.

E-paper always has a lag, but this goes beyond that. I first found out how frustrating this lag was when I needed to enter a 16-character Wi-Fi passcode. Switching from uppercase to lowercase was tedious, and the delay when switching the keyboard to numeric mode made me think it wasn’t working properly. It was; I just wasn’t giving it time before jabbing some more.

In a recent development, this lag also reduced my ability to read transcriptions on the device. It was quicker, easier, and less frustrating to look at them on my iPhone because using the Verso’s display felt like going back to an old Kindle Paperwhite (in a bad way).

This slowness never got better, and I never got used to it. As a result, it undermines the usefulness of the touchscreen as both a display and a user input method. This is a shame because it’s a really neat feature that might keep me off my phone more, but that half-second delay between tap and reaction was too much for me. That’s the way of it with devices that have to be power-efficient. Processing power is always the first thing to be sacrificed.

Also: I’ve owned 50+ power stations – one number matters most.

Sources indicate that bottom line: I found myself getting frustrated by how slow the Verso was, especially when tapping the screen or pressing the buttons. It all felt too hit-and-miss. The Note Pro might have been just as slow behind the scenes, but there was no display to give me that feedback. Also, everything was done either with a button press or through the app. And since I’ve always got my phone with me, this is no hardship.

The Verso could also be simplified by removing the “Ask Flowtica” button. I don’t see the point of a separate physical button for a feature I already have on plenty of other devices. And to make things worse, it was painfully slow to use.

Also: 5 USB cables that can fry hardware and steal your data – or worse.

I could whip out my phone, open a browser, and type my question — and quite possibly another two or three — and get an answer while Flowtica was still thinking.

Recent findings suggest that I also received a few “no internet connection” messages with the Verso, and no, my internet connection was fine (I did try it on several Wi-Fi networks, with similar results). Maybe these complications are specific to my device, or maybe they’ll be resolved with future software updates, but these connectivity dropouts certainly got in the way of using the Verso.

The Note Pro just worked. The one button did what it was supposed to do, and there were never any concerns moving recordings from the device to the cloud for transcription.

There’s little point in spending money on an AI voice recorder if you’re not going to use AI to process that raw audio and output it as something useful.

Also: I tried a $200 smartwatch with voice recording – how it beat the Apple Watch.

Sources indicate that both devices come with unlimited transcription, but both companies put limits on how much of the “advanced” features you can use before you have to put skin in the game and buy a subscription. For the Verso, live on-screen transcription, Voice ID, and summaries are advanced features that are limited to 300 minutes a month for those not on a subscription proposal.

If this feels somewhat confusing — and you’re not alone — the easiest way to think about it is that Comulytic’s free tier includes unlimited basic summaries, while Verso’s main screen feature is metered.

The Flowtica Verso hits the market with a list price of $299. That’s a steep premium to pay for that e-paper display compared to the competition. And it feels even steeper when the lag gets in the way as much as it did.

The Comulytic Note Pro is under $130, which is about as cheap as it gets for a good AI voice recorder. Even the biggest name in the game, the Plaud Note Pro, is only $189.

Also: Google is making it easier to opt out of Gemini AI model training.

In a recent development, if I didn’t feel like I was fighting the lag on almost everything I did with the Verso, I’d stick with it. But it’s frustrating, and it’s far easier to slip back into old habits. It’s possible future updates will streamline the Verso’s UI, but if you’re someone who finds it hard to wait half a second for something to happen, it could feel frustrating and is the reason why I’m sticking with the Note Pro for now.

Finally, be aware that subscriptions come into play on both devices, and that the Verso’s screen offers metered free usage for what it calls “AI minutes” before requiring a monthly payment.

#21760. Latest Update: Google makes it easier to use Gemini without training AI on your data

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (553 w)

Latest Update: Google makes it easier to use Gemini without training AI on your data

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (553 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, it can be hard to use Google products—or even the Internet itself—without coming into contact with Gemini AI.
  • Sources indicate that the change currently rolling out to Gemini will separate your chat history from training, which allows you to retain basic AI functionality without handing Google quite so much control over your data.
  • According to recent reports, as the latest settings roll out, owners will see separate toggles for model training and chat history.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, it can be hard to use Google products—or even the Internet itself—without coming into contact with Gemini AI. That is, of course, by design. The more you use Gemini, the more data Google collects to train and improve its generative AI chatbot. The options to limit training on your data have been scant, but Google is finally adding more controls to the Gemini app.

Sources indicate that the change currently rolling out to Gemini will separate your chat history from training, which allows you to retain basic AI functionality without handing Google quite so much control over your data. Prior to this change, the only way to opt out of contributing your chat contents (including attachments) for training was to turn off your history. That made it impossible to go back and pick up a chat down the road.

According to recent reports, as the latest settings roll out, owners will see separate toggles for model training and chat history. The history setting will continue to support an adjustable limit, but you will no longer have to change it to stop Google from training on your Gemini usage. Meanwhile, AI training will be an opt-out situation. You’ll need to find the toggle to block Google from using your chats for AI training. It’s under Activity in the Gemini settings. You can also access the menu from your Google account under Data and Privacy > My Activity > Other activity > Gemini Apps Activity.

Importantly, this only applies to future interactions with Gemini. If you have previously fed any data into Google’s AI, that’s already part of the training data. That can include your inputs, Gemini’s responses, uploaded files, tool calls, your location, and data from connected apps. Google notes it may retain this data for up to three years to improve its models. The manufacturer has previously noted it attempts to filter personal information out of the Gemini activity history, but that isn’t a guarantee.

Regardless of your chosen activity settings, you can always manually remove anything you don’t want saved on the same page with the history and training toggles. However, reviewed chats that are already part of the training data won’t be retroactively deleted. Opting out of training doesn’t mean Google won’t have your data, either. Google may use this data in other ways for up to three years—it just won’t add it to AI-training data sets.

Industry observers note that if you want to use Gemini and not retain any data, your options are actually a bit more limited now. Currently, if you disable history, Google still retains that data for 72 hours (and 24 hours for the user). Once the updated page is live, this duration will change to two months. So you can access that data for longer, but so can Google. The firm says this is to “respond to you, process your feedback, and protect Google, its users, and the public.” Essentially, Google will be more able to identify nefarious AI usage even if someone disables history.

Industry observers note that even with the longer chat retention, the ability to control AI training is still a welcome privacy improvement. Google states the change is rolling out globally, but it may take a few weeks to show up for everyone.

“Trump was in bed with Jensen”: Critics balk at Huang’s wish to return to Nvidia

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1982 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On Monday, large trucks began circling the streets of Washington, DC, carrying billboards urging Congress to investigate the Trump administration’s ties with Nvidia’s disgraced CEO Jensen Huang.
  • “Jensen was in bed with a spy from China,” the billboards created by the Tech Oversight Project (TOP) alleged.
  • According to recent reports, currently, Trump is supporting a campaign to bring back Huang as Nvidia’s CEO—despite many Republicans calling it a “horrible idea.” Breaking his silence, Huang issued a statement Tuesday saying he would be “honored” to return, but the board said reinstatement is not under consideration as an internal investigation into US spying claims remains ongoing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Monday, large trucks began circling the streets of Washington, DC, carrying billboards urging Congress to investigate the Trump administration’s ties with Nvidia’s disgraced CEO Jensen Huang.

“Jensen was in bed with a spy from China,” the billboards created by the Tech Oversight Project (TOP) alleged. “Trump was in bed with Jensen.” TOP is a nonprofit that describes itself as “dedicated to reining in Substantial Tech.”.

According to recent reports, currently, Trump is supporting a campaign to bring back Huang as Nvidia’s CEO—despite many Republicans calling it a “horrible idea.” Breaking his silence, Huang issued a statement Tuesday saying he would be “honored” to return, but the board said reinstatement is not under consideration as an internal investigation into US spying claims remains ongoing. Huang used the moment to say that his interests align with the US’s, saying:.

I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. Nvidia has been my life’s work. Building it into the organization it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like Nvidia be possible. I love our country, and I love Nvidia.

Trump may have learned as early as this spring that Huang was potentially the target of Chinese espionage, but the president claimed recently that he didn’t know Huang was potentially exposed to a Chinese spy as he was becoming a prominent part of Trump’s inner circle, CNN reported.

In a recent development, if Trump wasn’t adequately briefed, it raises question about whether the White House acted with “sufficient urgency” to address a serious espionage threat, CNN said. But if Trump is deflecting, an even “graver question” will emerge about why Trump didn’t act on information and instead continued to keep Huang close, CNN said.

Instead of distancing himself from the Nvidia CEO, Trump invited Huang to sit at the head table during a state dinner with China’s president Xi Jinping, and last month, Trump awarded Huang the National Medal of Science, the nation’s highest scientiﬁc honor, for his AI achievements.

In a recent development, “Not only has he continued to do nothing, he’s invited that very CEO into the White House and on state visits to China with him,” Sacha Haworth, TOP’s founder and CEO, told Ars. “And the question we all have to ask is ‘why on Earth would he do that?’”.

What Trump and Nvidia knew—and when—have become central questions for some Republicans, as well as top Democrats who proposal to investigate the scandal when they assume control of key committees in Congress next year. Andrew Yoon, head of research for a nonprofit called CivAI, which warns the public of dangers from AI, told Ars that Huang doesn’t need to be compromised by China to have endangered the US. Prioritizing boosting profits over national security alone is “pretty concerning.”.

In a recent development, “I think the most notable thing here is that Jensen Huang has been at the absolute forefront of lobbying to be able to sell chips to China,” Yoon remarked. “He has leveraged his very deep relationships with government, especially President Trump, in order to be able to sell as many Nvidia chips to China as he can get away with. If he could be selling Blackwell chips to China, I’m sure he would be.”.

Yoon noted that evidence suggests some Chinese AI models have been trained on Blackwell chips. Even with China’s push to prioritize domestic chipmakers like Huawei, Nvidia chips remain “indispensable” to China’s frontier AI goals, Yoon remarked. And national security experts fear that access to high-end chips will help China advance its military AI or gain economic ground.

The White House isn’t commenting on Trump’s relationship with Huang. Among the lawmakers accusing the Trump administration of “corruption” is Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), The Wall Street Journal reported. He has already asked the White House to “preserve all communications” between Trump and Huang.

In a recent development, other lawmakers are “seeking more information about what Trump knew about the relationship between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang,” the former Megaspeed CEO whom Huang admitted to having an affair with. They also want to know more about “the administration’s failure to stop artiﬁcial-intelligence chips from going to China,” WSJ reported, and Nvidia’s reportedly $25 million donation to the White House ballroom.

“It is not just an intelligence issue; it’s also a potential corruption issue,” Blumenthal mentioned. “There needs to be a really penetrating, comprehensive investigation of all the possible compromises of our intelligence that may have occurred, but also… that Donald Trump is so high on the head of Nvidia, and now is potentially linked to intelligence compromises.”.

In a recent development, trump has profited off Nvidia’s success while in office, buying “millions of dollars worth of Nvidia shares in his personal brokerage accounts since returning to oﬃce in 2025,” the WSJ reported. The White House maintains that the president has no role in managing his stock portfolio.

According to recent reports, other officials advising Trump on AI also benefited from relaxing export curbs, TOP stated. On Tuesday, the group issued a report summarizing what the public knows about potential conflicts of interest of two Trump officials: former White House AI Czar David Sacks and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.

Haworth, TOP’s founder, told Ars she’s concerned that Sacks and Lutnick abused their power to convince Trump to let Nvidia sell cutting-edge technology to China, while standing to “gain astronomical amounts of money.”.

“The public is outraged by Nvidia’s CEO for compromising our national security, but we didn’t get here because of Jensen Huang’s missteps alone,” Haworth said. If “Nvidia was knowingly doing business with companies tied to illegal chip sales and smuggling with China,” then “the Trump administration was asleep at the wheel,” she said.

“White House AI Czar David Sacks and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick were protecting their own fortunes rather than looking out for Americans,” Haworth said.

If the US fails to hold them accountable for alleged conflicts of interest, “it would send a signal that powerful men once again cannot be held to account and that powerful men are protecting powerful men,” Haworth said.

Industry observers note that detailing Sacks’ alleged conflicts, the group cited Latest York Times reporting that the former AI czar had long supported Huang’s stance that allowing Nvidia to sell more chips in China would help the US stay ahead in the AI race. After Sacks became Trump’s key AI advisor, Huang quickly forged a “tight bond” with him, and “both stood to benefit” from their push to sell chips to China, TOP reported.

It has been revealed that also notably, while advising the White House, Sacks opposed policies such as the Trump administration’s recent move to cut off China’s remote access to US-made chips through now-restricted Southeast Asian data centers. Citing Sacks’ alignment with Huang, TOP reported that after just one meeting with the two men, Trump decided to allow Nvidia to sell AI chips to China that the Biden administration had previously blocked.

According to recent reports, huang valued his alliance with Sacks, TOP noted, citing reporting that showed Huang declaring last year that Nvidia was “lucky” to have Sacks advising Trump. But TOP is concerned that the alliance was built on mutual financial interest and that Sacks took a part-time role in the Trump administration to avoid divestments or disclosure requirements that might have revealed the extent of his possible conflicts of interest.

TOP flagged two areas it believes warrant Congressional investigation. While advising Trump to embrace AI deregulation, Sacks and his firm, Craft Ventures, continued investing substantially in AI. Sacks also stood to benefit from pushing Trump to integrate AI into warfare and national security tools, TOP’s report stated. Craft Ventures has invested in Palantir, “a Peter Thiel-founded government contractor seen as a ‘rising star’ in the US Defense Tech World and holding hundreds of millions in US government defense contracts,” TOP said.

Even within the Trump administration, officials have turned on Commerce Secretary Lutnick, seemingly looking to blame him for mishandling the Nvidia spying investigation and allowing Trump to maintain close ties with Huang despite apparent intelligence risks.

Lutnick has bragged publicly that he promised Huang “really easy access to the President” after joining the administration, TOP reported. That alliance helped push Trump to approve the sale of Nvidia H200s to China, TOP said. And that seemed to directly benefit Lutnick, TOP said, because before he was confirmed as secretary, he was CEO of Cantor Fitzgerald, which held $1.2 billion in Nvidia stock.

In a recent development, “In his role as Secretary, Lutnick is responsible for policing exports of sensitive technology to adversaries and global rivals, like China,” TOP reported. “Lutnick and the organization he controls benefited greatly from opening sales of Nvidia chips to China.”.

After Lutnick was required to hand that tech giant over to his son, Cantor Fitzgerald “maintained extensive commercial ties to Nvidia, helping arrange billions of dollars in financing for companies in its AI business universe and repeatedly hosting its top executives,” TOP noted.

It has been revealed that those investments shifted substantially around the same time that Lutnick began facing pressure to “crack down on Megaspeed, a Singapore-based manufacturer suspected of funneling Nvidia’s advanced artificial intelligence chips to China,” TOP reported. Cantor Fitzgerald “reduced its Nvidia holdings by nearly 50 percent between September 2025 and March 2026,” TOP said.

In a recent development, however, when Trump was reportedly first told of the spying allegations this spring, Cantor Fitzgerald again continued to boost Nvidia. Most prominently, the company helped “finance the expansion of one of Nvidia’s newest business partners, IREN,” facilitating a five-year, $3.4 billion deal between Nvidia and the Australia-based cloud computing provider.

Sources indicate that among those now criticizing Lutnick for weak enforcement of export controls that appeared designed to protect Huang’s bottom line is Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. But even with scrutiny coming from within the Trump administration, not everyone is convinced that Lutnick did anything wrong. Yoon suggested that, given Lutnick’s long career, there may be normal explanations for potential financial conflicts.

“Maybe a separate question is ‘should people with a long storied history in business and industry be working in government at this level?’” Yoon stated.

Haworth said the next 48 hours will be critical in determining whether Huang succeeds in returning to Nvidia.

“I think it’s going to be incumbent on the incoming Democratic leadership to insist that whether or not he returns, investigations will follow,” Haworth said.

But Yoon thinks Nvidia is unlikely to bring Huang back any time soon, despite current evidence suggesting that “Nvidia’s actions here have been perfectly legal” and that “influencing a political system for your financial interests is very much legal in the United States.”.

Recent findings suggest that it seems “untenable for Nvidia to continue doing what they’re doing,” Yoon said. Zooming out even more, he suggested the scandal showed that the entire AI industry can no longer afford to operate under a profit motive alone, so long as governments continue positioning the technology as a strategic asset.

If US investigations expose corruption, bribery, treason, or other crimes, Nvidia risks losing some of its dominant stake in the GPU market. On Tuesday, The Information reported that some Nvidia customers had already lost trust and were looking to Google and AMD for more stability.

Nvidia has also been accused of intervening in a Commerce investigation, which Yoon noted could also be “pretty consequential” if any evidence bears that out.

Industry observers note that “I think it’s pretty unlikely that Huang makes it back to Nvidia any time soon,” Yoon said. “Maybe he goes on a redemption tour and comes back in five years or something, but I’m not really seeing a path forward for him right now.”.
